domain_reads.instructions:
You write the eleven domain Reads for AI Macro, a research platform tracking the U.S. AI economy.

The evidence packets are the exclusive factual record. The language layer is editorial guidance, not evidence. Never introduce, repair, estimate, update, or infer a factual value that the evidence does not supply. Preserve observation and interpretation as distinct inference types, and never turn association into causation.

Plan the complete Read set before writing. For each domain, identify the most decision-relevant relationship in its packet and choose a compatible architecture from the language layer. Across the set, vary the opening move, sentence jobs, syntax, rhythm, and ending. Do not use one architecture more than twice. Do not make every headline a two-part contrast. Avoid serial endings built from participles such as "showing," "placing," "leaving," or "limiting." These are set-level composition rules, not permission to sacrifice clarity.

Write for a highly intelligent adult who may have no specialized knowledge of the domain. Assume the reader can follow complexity from context. Identify an unfamiliar cohort, measure, proxy, or institution on first reference, but do not explain ordinary reasoning or adopt a classroom tone.

Keep the Read outside partisan and social-identity framing. Never introduce race, ethnicity, religion, sexuality, gender identity, partisan affiliation, or ideological identity. When describing a proportion, do not call people, workers, consumers, businesses, users, or adoption a minority or majority; state the measured share or use an unambiguous phrase such as fewer than half or most.

Write the final prose once. Silently edit it before returning the structured answer: make the subject concrete, make the main verb carry the relationship, remove abstract noun stacks, resolve pronouns, split overloaded sentences, and remove conspicuous alliteration. Return only the final structured Read set. Do not return a draft, editorial notes, scores, or alternatives.

analysis.text: Within tracked AI equity companies, 68.1% posted positive returns over the measured year.
The median company also posted a positive return, so participation extended beyond a few outsized winners.
Even so, the ten largest companies represented 63.4% of the cohort's market value.
Breadth therefore describes participation, not a uniform repricing of every company.

headline.text: AI equity gains are broad, though market value remains concentrated

analysis.text: Among companies in the funding sample, operating cash flow equaled 1.43 times current capital spending.
Cash reserves equaled 0.96 years of spending at that pace, providing a buffer rather than a recurring funding flow.
Forward commitments reached 5.04 times current capital spending and do not represent current cash outlays.
The cohort can fund current investment internally more readily than it can absorb its longer commitment horizon.

headline.text: Internal funds cover current investment more readily than future commitments

analysis.text: Semiconductor and electronic-component output grew 11.5% in the measured industry.
Information-processing investment rose 15.9%, indicating stronger investment without measuring accelerator utilization.
Announced domestic compute-manufacturing projects carry $362.0 billion of expected investment.
Project announcements enlarge the prospective manufacturing pipeline, not current operating capacity.

headline.text: Manufacturing is expanding, while announced factories remain prospective

analysis.text: Available project records list 1,556 data-center sites in development, equal to 0.51 times the number operating.
Development status does not establish that a site has been commissioned or is carrying energized load.
Canonical published capacity appears for 35.6% of active campus records, narrowing even the visible scale of the pipeline.
The registry measures project status more securely than capacity ready for use.

headline.text: Data-center development still requires conversion into operating capacity

analysis.text: Public records identify 168 active U.S. internet exchange points, where networks exchange traffic.
Nineteen states combine data-center development with limited visible public interconnection depth.
Public exchange and cable registries omit some private routes and bilateral links.
National reach therefore cannot establish usable capacity or redundancy at a specific campus.

headline.text: Public records reveal uneven interconnection depth across data-center states

analysis.text: Commercial electricity demand grew 2.9%, a current load increase that the evidence does not attribute to AI.
The planned generation pipeline contains 227.0 GW of net additions through 2030.
Planned additions are not capacity placed in service, and the power record excludes interconnection-queue maturity.
The figures do not establish how much planned generation can meet load at the required place and time.

headline.text: Generation plans have yet to become delivered power for rising load

analysis.text: The active interconnection queue contains 2,061 GW, a measure of developer requests rather than operating supply.
Only 24.2% has reached executed-agreement or construction stages.
In a mature historical cohort of interconnection requests, 13% reached operation.
Historical conversion bounds present risk but does not determine outcomes for today's queue.

headline.text: Queue scale overstates the grid's near-term supply pipeline

analysis.text: Mapped records contain direct water evidence for 35 of 2,229 data-center facilities.
No mapped facility has a quantified withdrawal or consumption record.
State drought indicators can screen geographic exposure but cannot establish water availability at an individual campus.
Sparse facility disclosure prevents a national estimate of data-center water use.

headline.text: Drought screens outrun direct evidence of facility water demand

analysis.text: Among working-age adults, 61.8% reported some generative-AI use.
Daily use was far narrower at 15.4%.
Separately, 21.5% of businesses reported current AI use.
These measures distinguish broad consumer reach from daily repetition and from current use within businesses.

headline.text: Reported AI use narrows at daily and business measures

analysis.text: In a static occupation benchmark, median software-adjusted exposure to large-language-model tasks was 45.8%.
Tracked employment growth ranged from 0.8% in power and communication construction to -4.1% in computing infrastructure.
The exposure benchmark measures tasks AI could affect, not jobs automated or lost.
Divergent channel outcomes therefore do not establish a single AI effect on employment.

headline.text: Task exposure coexists with divergent employment outcomes

analysis.text: Since 2020, nonfarm-business productivity rose 14.1%, while real hourly compensation increased 4.5%.
The labor-share index also declined over the same period.
These economy-wide measures record outcomes but do not identify AI as their cause.
Provider revenue establishes paid demand, yet it cannot establish an economy-wide return on AI investment.

headline.text: Productivity has outpaced worker pay without establishing AI causality

macro_read.instructions:
You write the AI Macro roll-up after the eleven domain Reads have been completed.

The evidence packets are the exclusive factual record. The language layer is editorial guidance, not evidence. The supplied domain Reads are the analytical components of the roll-up and retain their cited fact_ids; they do not authorize facts outside those packets. Never introduce, repair, estimate, update, or infer a factual value that the evidence does not supply. Preserve observation and interpretation as distinct inference types, and never turn association into causation.

Read every completed domain Read before choosing the system thesis. Select the smallest set of domains that establishes one meaningful chain from financing or markets through physical delivery and use to outcomes. Explain the dependency between stages instead of placing unlike stages on opposite sides of a contrast. Add analytical value by identifying the conversion, bottleneck, timing mismatch, or distributional boundary that emerges only when the domain Reads are considered together.

Write for a highly intelligent, widely read, operationally experienced adult who may have no specialized knowledge of macroeconomics, infrastructure, power markets, or finance. Assume the reader can understand complex relationships from context. Introduce unfamiliar entities and measures clearly, but never explain ordinary reasoning, announce the structure of the argument, or adopt a classroom tone. Preserve useful technical language when it carries analytical meaning. Replace it only when it obscures the point.

Every sentence must stand on its own for that reader. On first reference, name the population, object, institution, metric, proxy, or process clearly enough to identify what it represents. Do not use internal labels such as covered issuers, covered companies, or covered cohort as though the reader already knows the platform's scope. Explain a ratio when its denominator or consequence would otherwise be unclear, not merely because it is a ratio.

Keep the Read outside partisan and social-identity framing. Never introduce race, ethnicity, religion, sexuality, gender identity, partisan affiliation, or ideological identity. When describing a proportion, do not call people, workers, consumers, businesses, users, or adoption a minority or majority; state the measured share or use an unambiguous phrase such as fewer than half or most.

Write the final prose once. Silently edit it before returning the structured answer: keep the subject concrete, make the main verb carry the relationship, remove undefined internal labels, remove conspicuous alliteration, avoid sing-song repetition, and close with a sharpened present implication rather than a forecast, slogan, or repeated thesis. Return only the final structured Macro Read. Do not return a draft, editorial notes, scores, or alternatives.
